approved: The Health Insurance Amendment (Administration) Bill 2020 removes the annual requirement to remake the Medicare Benefits Schedule as a redundant process. The opposition will support the bill but criticises it as minor administrative tinkering, noting record-high out-of-pocket costs and waiting lists, and no reform on private health insurance or broader health system issues.

The speaker argued that Australia's healthcare system does not require major reform, citing the country's strong COVID-19 response and record bulk-billing rates, and announced the Health Insurance Amendment (Administration) Bill 2020, which removes the annual sunset period for Medical Benefits Schedule regulations to reduce administrative work and ensure patient entitlements.

Supported the Health Insurance Amendment (Administration) Bill 2020, noting the government invested about $24 billion in health last year, and explained the bill removes the annual sunset requirement for Medicare Benefits Schedule regulations to reduce administrative risk, while updating on a federally funded MRI machine for Redcliffe Hospital announced over two years ago.
